details: Bitcoin climbed to a two-and-a-half-month high, surpassing $78,000, with Ethereum also seeing significant gains. This rally is largely attributed to easing geopolitical tensions after the Strait of Hormuz was declared "open and ready for business," alongside sustained inflows into spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs). The improved sentiment is also supported by recent net inflows from Bitcoin whales, suggesting a potential end to their distribution phase.
title: Bitcoin Surges Past $78K on Hormuz Reopening & ETF Inflows

details: The anticipated release of the legislative text for the US crypto market structure bill has been postponed. Deliberations are ongoing for critical provisions, including regulations for stablecoin yield, anti-money laundering (AML) measures, and decentralized finance (DeFi). This delay underscores the complex challenges in establishing comprehensive and clear regulatory frameworks for the cryptocurrency sector.
title: US Crypto Bill Delayed Amid Stablecoin Yield & AML Debates

details: Iran has reportedly begun demanding cryptocurrency as payment for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial global shipping artery. This development highlights the increasing use of digital assets in geopolitical contexts and raises concerns regarding their potential role in facilitating sanctions evasion and illicit financing networks.
title: Iran Seeks Crypto Tolls for Strait of Hormuz Access

details: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) kept its federal funds target range unchanged at 3.50%-3.75% during its March 17-18 meeting. While not a new decision, recent analysis indicates this stance continues to shape global liquidity and the cost of capital, directly impacting cryptocurrency markets. The Fed noted a solid pace of economic expansion and persistent, elevated inflation, implying a prolonged period of current interest rate conditions without immediate aggressive easing.
title: Fed Maintains Rates, Signals Steady Economic Pace
